subject: Post-call: VPC networking & performance SLOs for AcmeHealth
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Jane Miller <jane.miller@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: VPC networking & performance SLOs for AcmeHealth

Thanks again for your time this morning — quick recap and next steps from our side. High-level items we captured on the call: 

- Target SLOs you outlined: 95th percentile tail latency <= 120ms for streaming responses (token-by-token), and p95 for non-streaming generation <= 200ms.
- Expected steady-state concurrency: ~2k concurrent streaming sessions with bursts to 4k for short windows.
- Throughput target: ~5k tokens/sec sustained across the pool, spike to ~12k tokens/sec during peak batch windows.
- Preferred private connectivity: VPC peering / Transit Gateway in us-west-2. VPN as fallback for DR.
- Egress: outgoing requests to endpoints will be NATed through your central egress account; you flagged possible egress cost sensitivity.

Attached is a short checklist we use for Private/VPC performance qualification (redwood-private-perf-checklist.pdf). From our side, immediate next steps: 
1) Aisha to follow up with an engineering checklist and required IP ranges/BGP expectations.
2) Schedule a 60-minute tech workshop to step through perf tests and peering setup (suggested window: Thu 2026-03-04 10:00 PT).
3) You to share the network diagram and confirmation of the target region and peering model.

If the numbers above need any correction, flag them and I will update the mutual action plan.

— Connor
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
From: Jane Miller <jane.miller@acmehealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajesh Patel <r.patel@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: VPC networking & performance SLOs for AcmeHealth

Connor — thanks for the clear write-up and the checklist. A few clarifications from our infra team: 

- Region: production workloads will run in aws-us-west-2.
- Connectivity: primary plan is Transit Gateway peering into our account (we manage BGP), VPN as fallback. We can provide BGP ASN and a contact for BGP session setup.
- Latency expectations: internal application budget is 80ms for request/response inside our VPC. End-to-end from client to your model runtime (including webrtc/ingest) we'd like p95 <= 150ms if possible. We noted your p95 targets; please confirm what we can expect on the Private deployment vs Hosted.
- Concurrency: target is 2k concurrent streams sustained; we can tolerate short spikes to 5k.
- Token throughput: we expect bursts up to ~10k tokens/sec for 30–60s windows; sustained 4–6k tokens/sec.

Attached our current network diagram (acme-network-diagram.png) and a preliminary peering request form — will fill formal peering paperwork once we agree on IP ranges and filtering.

Questions from our side:
1) Does Redwood require TLS termination on the edge, or can we terminate TLS in our egress and use mTLS to your runtime?
2) Any recommendations on MTU or keepalive tweaks for stable streaming over Transit Gateway?
3) Can you estimate incremental egress cost per TB if traffic flows through our NAT?

Happy to run the tech workshop on Thu if you can share an agenda.

— Jane
Jane Miller
Director, Infrastructure — Acme Health
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Jane Miller <jane.miller@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: VPC networking & performance SLOs for AcmeHealth

Looping in a few technical points we need to validate before the workshop. Jane — quick answers requested so we can prep an environment and perf harness: 

1) Exact peering model: Transit Gateway peering (yes/no) and will you accept our source IP ranges for inbound from the TGW? We will provide a /20 block for the Redwood runtime egress.
2) BGP: if you can provide ASN, customer edge IPs, and a preferred hold-time, we can draft a BGP config.
3) NAT/egress: confirm whether your NAT is centralized (single account) or per-VPC. Central NATs can add ~2–6ms on average; we need to budget that into overall p95 if traffic is NATed.
4) TLS termination: Redwood supports mTLS to the runtime endpoint; we do not require termination on your side. If you plan to terminate TLS within your VPC, we'll need to establish a secure hop (mTLS or private CA).
5) Path MTU: recommend 1436–1452 to be safe for jumbo-safe networks; if you have enforced smaller MTU we'll adapt.

Perf validation plan we propose for the workshop: 
- 30-minute sustained streaming test at target concurrency (2k sessions) with token emission rate to reach ~5k tokens/sec.
- 5-minute spike tests to 5k concurrent sessions and 10k tokens/sec to validate graceful degradation and fallback.
- Measure p50/p90/p95/p99 for both streaming per-token latency and end-to-end request latency.
- Capture tcpdump + netstat snapshots and per-connection RTT (we'll provide collection scripts).

Can you confirm availability for Thu 2026-03-04 10:00 PT? If not, propose two alternatives. We'll prepare the perf harness and share a runbook ahead of time.

— Aisha
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
aisha_rahman@redwood.com
From: Rajesh Patel <r.patel@acmehealth.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Jane Miller <jane.miller@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T11:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: VPC networking & performance SLOs for AcmeHealth

Thanks — confirmed: us-west-2.

A couple of answers from the network team: 
- NAT is centralized in our security account (single egress path). We'll attach the formal peering-request-form.pdf with required approvals (attached).
- We'll provide BGP ASN and two peer IPs by EOD 2026-03-03.
- We target effective internal application latency of ~80ms; adding the centralized NAT we expect +3–6ms.
- For TLS: we prefer to terminate TLS on our side and use mTLS to Redwood endpoints — we can share a cert signing workflow for the mTLS certs.
- Egress: rough estimate — $95/TB in our current model; please provide your bandwidth/egress calc so we can model it for budget.

We'll plan to have our cloud network engineer on the Thu workshop.

— Rajesh
Network Engineering, Acme Health
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Jane Miller <jane.miller@acmehealth.com>, Rajesh Patel <r.patel@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: VPC networking & performance SLOs for AcmeHealth

Perfect — thanks for the details and the fast turnaround. Summary & agreed next steps: 

1) Workshop confirmed: Thu 2026-03-04 10:00 PT — agenda to include peering/BGP, perf-harness run, and telemetry collection. Aisha will share the runbook and data collection scripts 24 hours prior. (Action: Aisha)
2) Rajesh to send BGP ASN + peer IPs by EOD 2026-03-03; after that we will generate our /20 source ranges and draft the peering ACLs. (Action: Rajesh + Connor)
3) Redwood to provide an initial estimate for egress bandwidth cost and incremental TB costs based on target throughput; we will include modeling for 4k tokens/sec sustained and 10k tokens/sec spikes. (Action: Vivek)
4) On perf targets: Redwood expects Private deployment runtime (pinned capacity) to comfortably meet p95 streaming per-token <= 120ms given the peering model — final numbers to be validated during the workshop.
5) Deliverables before workshop: runbook link (Drive), perf checklist (attached), and peering ACL draft.

I'll send calendar invites and a short Mutual Action Plan after we get the BGP details. Thanks all — looking forward to the workshop.

— Connor
